item.title: Ozzy Osbourne Once Said He Wanted a Beatles Song Played at His Funeral
item.description: English singer and songwriter Ozzy Osbourne, best known as the original frontman of Black Sabbath and for his solo career under his own name, died on Tuesday, July 22, at the age of 76.

item.title: The Guitarist ANGUS YOUNG Once Blamed For Setting ROCK MUSIC Back Two Decades: 'Jeez, It Sounds So Dated'
item.description: Angus Young , the longtime AC/DC guitarist, is known for his stripped-down style, blistering riffs, and no-nonsense views on what makes a good guitar player. Over the years, he’s made his opinion clear about effects pedals, tremolo bars, and overly polished guitar work.

item.title: Mötley Crüe bassist NIKKI SIXX Explains DOLLY PARTON Collab: 'She Was a Hard Yes'
item.description: Mötley Crüe and Dolly Parton have released a new version of Home Sweet Home to mark the song’s 40th anniversary. The track debuted at No. 1 on the Mediabase Classic Rock Songs chart in June.

item.title: Watch AC/DC Live in Düsseldorf Featuring Angus Young, Brian Johnson, and New Touring Members
item.description: Hard rock icons AC/DC played to a packed stadium in Düsseldorf, Germany, on July 8. The concert took place at Merkur Spiel-Arena as part of the band’s summer 2025 leg of the “Power Up” European tour.

item.title: JACK BLACK Covers 'MR. CROWLEY' with Young Rock Musicians in Tribute to OZZY OSBOURNE; VIDEO
item.description: Jack Black paid tribute to Ozzy Osbourne with a dramatic performance of “Mr. Crowley”, recorded on video and played during the Back to the Beginning event in Birmingham, England, on Saturday, July 5.

item.title: The One Band CHRIS CORNELL Believed Was America’s Answer To LED ZEPPELIN
item.description: Long before grunge made Seattle famous, Chris Cornell had already picked his local musical heroes. Among British rock influences, there was one American band he saw as a standout.

item.title: The Song JAMES HETFIELD Considers the Greatest of All, and Countless Bands Have Tried to Recreate
item.description: James Hetfield has always worn his influences on his sleeve. In a recent episode of The Metallica Report (transcribed by LOUDLEGENDS.COM), the Metallica frontman named Led Zeppelin’s “Stairway to Heaven” as the greatest song of all time.

item.title: AC/DC Opens European Tour in Prague, Czech President Attends; VIDEOS
item.description: AC/DC launched the summer leg of their “Power Up” European tour Thursday night in Prague, Czech Republic. The concert took place at Letiště Praha Letňany and drew an estimated crowd of 60,000 people.

item.title: AC/DC Adds More Australian Shows As Fans Struggle With Ticket Website Issues
item.description: AC/DC has added three new dates to its upcoming Power Up tour in Australia. The new shows are scheduled for: November 16 in Melbourne at Melbourne Cricket Ground November 25 in Sydney at Accor Stadium December 18 in Brisbane at Suncorp Stadium Fans can find tickets and all official dates at acdc.

item.title: OZZY OSBOURNE Says He Wants To Work With PAUL MCCARTNEY: 'I Would Be Honoured'
item.description: During a new episode of Ozzy Speaks on SiriusXM (transcribed by LOUDLEGENDS.COM), Ozzy Osbourne mentioned that he would like to collaborate with Paul McCartney. The rock icon discussed the idea while chatting with his co-host, Billy Morrison.

item.title: Mick Ralphs, Co-Founder of Bad Company and Mott the Hoople, Dies at 81
item.description: Mick Ralphs, the guitarist and songwriter who helped shape the sound of classic rock with Bad Company and Mott the Hoople, has died at age 81. He is survived by his partner, Susie Chavasse, his two sons, three stepchildren, and his longtime bandmates Paul Rodgers and Simon Kirke.

item.title: AC/DC Faces Backlash Over Viral Tour Footage As Fans Call For Retirement: 'Painful'
item.description: Footage from a recent AC/DC concert is making waves online, and not in the way the band might hope. A TikTok video from the group’s May 4 performance at Gillette Stadium in Foxborough, Massachusetts, has gone viral (watch it below).

item.title: AC/DC Announces 2025 Stadium Tour of Australia With Amyl and The Sniffers
item.description: AC/DC is heading back to their roots. The legendary Australian rock band has announced a five-city stadium tour across the country for November and December 2025. This will be their first Australian tour in ten years.

item.title: The Unusual Way AC/DC's ANGUS YOUNG Came Up With the Chorus of 'HIGHWAY TO HELL'
item.description: Angus Young, lead guitarist and founding member of AC/DC, shared a rather unexpected story about how he wrote one of rock’s most iconic choruses. Speaking in a 2021 interview with Essentials Radio on Apple Music (via Kerrang), Young explained how the chorus of “Highway to Hell” came to him, not in a studio or during rehearsal, but while he was on a bathroom break.

item.title: The 'COMMERCIAL' Song AC/DC Didn’t Want To Record, And It Ended Up On The Charts
item.description: In June 1978, AC/DC got their first taste of chart action in the UK with “Rock ’n’ Roll Damnation”, which reached number 24. Nothing to throw a parade over, but for a band that had never cracked the charts there before, it was a decent showing.

item.title: The One AC/DC Song ANGUS YOUNG Struggles to Play Live
item.description: Few bands are as famously built on no-nonsense riffs as AC/DC. For Angus Young and his brother Malcolm, there was no mystery to their formula: loud guitars, open chords, and choruses made for the crowd to scream in unison.

item.title: RINGO STARR Slams ROGER DALTREY Over Firing Of Son: 'Never Liked How That Little Man Runs The Band'
item.description: Zak Starkey didn’t bother hiding his disappointment after being pushed out of The Who, a gig he held for nearly 30 years as the band’s live drummer. It all unraveled after a messy show at the Royal Albert Hall earlier this year, which ultimately triggered the official announcement of his departure in April.

item.title: AC/DC Reportedly Planning Final Concerts For Late 2025 In Australia
item.description: According to behind-the-scenes information obtained by Blunt magazine, AC/DC is expected to announce what could be the final concerts of their career, scheduled for late 2025 (Get AC/DC Tickets Here).

item.title: DUFF MCKAGAN Compares OZZY OSBOURNE to Lemmy, Prince, and Iggy Pop
item.description: Duff McKagan has seen plenty of rock stars come and go, but when it comes to Ozzy Osbourne, he doesn’t mince words. “A constant in rock and roll,” as he puts it.

item.title: Far-Right Politician Tries to Cancel SLIPKNOT and JUDAS PRIEST Shows in Italy
item.description: Alcide Mosso, a member of Italy’s far-right Lega Nord party, has launched an attack on the Ferrara Summer Festival, held throughout the summer in the city of Ferrara.

item.title: Ted Nugent on His Never-Ending Tour Life: “I Never Used the R-Word”
item.description: Ted Nugent, 76 years old and still grinding away, is back on stage after his farewell tour. Not because he changed his mind. Because, according to him, he never used the word retire.

item.title: Jethro Tull’s Ian Anderson Slams Brazilian Fans & iPhones: "Crowds Are Worse Than Ever"
item.description: So Ian Anderson, flute-wielding sorcerer of JETHRO TULL, has had it with you people—yes, YOU, the one recording an entire concert through a cracked iPhone 8 with 2% battery while also screaming “PLAY THICK AS A BRICK!

item.title: Ozzy Osbourne “Can’t Walk,” But His Legendary Voice Remains Untouched, Says Sharon
item.description: Alright, so Ozzy Osbourne—THE Prince of Darkness—is out here casually defying medical science. The dude CANNOT WALK. But he CAN STILL BELT OUT “CRAZY TRAIN” LIKE IT’S 1980.

item.title: Lorraine Lewis on Joining OnlyFans: "It’s Sexy, I’m Owning It, And I’m Having Fun!"
item.description: Lorraine Lewis. 66 years old. Rock icon. Ex-VIXEN. Current FEMME FATALE badass. Also? Now officially on OnlyFans. And not just dipping her toes in—she’s fully in the pool.

item.title: The End of an Era: Ozzy Osbourne’s Final Performance with Black Sabbath Announced
item.description: You ever notice how bands never actually retire? They announce their very last, totally final, we swear on our drummer’s snare collection concert… and then five years later—boom.
